This PR extends the one for Ridge (still WIP, #27800) to use the array API in `RidgeCV` and `RidgeClassifierCV` (when cv="gcv")

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.

this could make those estimators faster as an important part of their computational cost is due to compute either an eigendecomposition of XX^T or an SVD of X

#### Any other comments?

The `_RidgeGCV` has numerical precision issues when computations are done in float32, which is why ATM in the main branch it always uses [float64](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/8f5ff3978fa9a6cc27868a30f22d5c12f0f59d03/sklearn/linear_model/_ridge.py#L1982)
I'm not sure what should be done for array API inputs on devices that do not have float64

not handled yet:
- [x] RidgeClassifierCV

comments.body:
Contrary to what I said in this morning meeting, I think we might want to implement the following logic:

- if the input namespace/device supports `xp.float64` upcasting, then do the upcast (as we currently do with NumPy)
- if not (e.g. pytorch + MPS device combination), accept that we have degraded numerical performance, adjust the tolerance in the tests accordingly and document this limited numerical precision guarantee in our Array API doc.


I think this is the strategy we are leaning towards in the review of #27113. During the review of the `r2_score` PR, I believe that @adrinjalali preferred that approach.

In a future PR, we might decide to drop the float32 -> float64 upcast in general for this estimator (as it silently triggers a potentially very large and unexpected memory allocation which is a usability problem in itself, even with NumPy) but I would rather make this decision independently of Array API support.
For my education: why is `v_prime` and `D` (respectively) not also passed to `get_namespace`? Is it worth a comment for future readers?
Where does it come up that `get_namespace` is called with something that leads to an exception from`array_api_compat.get_namespace()`? Is it when `X` is a sparse matrix/array?

yes when X is sparse:

```python
from scipy import sparse
import array_api_compat

array_api_compat.get_namespace(sparse.eye(3, format='csr'))
```

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
TypeError: csr_matrix is not a supported array type
```

I should probably check that explicitly rather than catching the exception
they are all computed during fit so barring any bugs they should all be in the same namespace (that of `X`) but you're right that it would be clearer to pass both to `get_namespace`

how would you recommend I check if the upcasting is possible? should I temporarily copy the `max_precision_float_dtype` and `supported_float_dtypes` changes from [27113](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/27113/files#diff-6264adab84df6fafdb2d950141783b52b718da1e1be773daae7b5921b2556f94R338) until it is merged? or is there already a utility in scikit-learn for checking that which I missed?
I think we should be explicit.
Feel free to copy with a TODO comment to remove redundant code once #27113 is merged to be able to decouple the 2 reviews.
I think one could write a lightweight narwhals version for array API
when we do the upcast with what precision should we store the coefficients and intercept? I guess for prediction we do not need the extra precision so we should use X's original dtype?
We already have `array_api_compat` and our own numpy wrapper that we could leverage to help us do that.

There is a new `array-api-extra` project that has started to implement missing utilities on top of what is standardized in the spec and therefore implemented in the `array-api-compat` project: 

https://data-apis.org/array-api-extra/

Actually, for this precise case, we already have `_NumPyAPIWrapper` that could (should?) be extended to add the `.linalg.vector_norm` alias for older NumPy versions that have not yet been aligned to the new API.

We can probably create a `_NumPyLinalgAPIWrapper` class with a `__getattr__` method to expose most symbols from `numpy.linalg` but also add the `vector_norm` alias.

I don't think I am a big fan of a factory function with a generic name such as `make_converter` that returns a callable for this pattern.

I think I would prefer a simple function such as:

```suggestion
        y, sample_weight = move_to_namespace_and_device(y, sample_weight, ref=X)
```
We could use our `_ravel` helper function to improve readability.

Wouldn't the following be enough?

```suggestion
        self.coef_ = dual_T @ X
```

I believe this is now handled in `_remove_non_arrays`.

```suggestion
    if not arrays:
```

If we want to go multi-line, I would rather simply do:

```suggestion
    namespace = array_api_compat.get_namespace(*arrays)
    is_array_api_compliant = True
```

but this change seems unrelated to the scope of this PR.
Similar remark as for `vector_norm`: this aliasing logic should be moved to `_NumPyAPIWrapper`.
We should use `get_namespace_and_device` here instead.
Maybe we can keep the callable factory pattern and just rename to `make_array_ns_and_device_mover`, as you prefer.

I am not sure if we still want to make `supported_float_dtypes` device sensitive: the new `_max_precision_float_dtype` in `main` does not delegate to `supported_float_dtypes` so we do not really have a case for this change anymore.
I'm not sure because X can be sparse. note on the main branch `safe_sparse_dot` is used -- but I'll check again
I think it works for 2D arrays/matrices.

```suggestion
- :class:`linear_model.RidgeCV` (see :ref:`device_support_for_float64`)
```

```suggestion
        # Using float32 can be numerically unstable for this estimator. So,
        # if the array API namespace and device allow, convert the input values
        # to float64 whenever possible before converting back the results to
        # float32 to keep prediction on float32 inputs efficient.
        dtype = _max_precision_float_dtype(xp, device=device_)
```
this can only be covered on devices where the max float precision is float32

there is a test [here](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/27961/files#diff-d0cf1401f90f9cff12a7dd9778bafb5d1a06137f4145be07c8530e2502af131fR673) to cover those lines (I checked it does locally) but only when both torch and array-api-strict are installed, is there such a configuration in one of the CI jobs?

The `xp.astype(decision > 0, max_float_dtype)` was previously hardcoded to 
`xp.astype(decision > 0, xp.float32)` but I decided to use the `max_float_dtype` instead. Let me know if we should instead revert back to `xp.float32`

I find it more natural to name `xp_y` the namespace of `y`. In the tests, `y_xp` stands for `y` moved to a namespace `xp` instead.

```suggestion
        xp_y, y_is_array_api = get_namespace(y)
        # TODO: Update this line to avoid calling `_convert_to_numpy`
        # once LabelBinarizer has been updated to accept non-NumPy array API
        # compatible inputs.
        Y = self._label_binarizer.fit_transform(
            _convert_to_numpy(y, xp_y) if y_is_array_api else y
        )
        Y = ensure_common_namespace_device(original_X, Y)[0]
        if y_is_array_api and xp_y.isdtype(y.dtype, "numeric"):
```

The following sounds enough:

```suggestion
            scores = 2.0 * xp.astype(decision > 0, decision.dtype) - 1.0
```

```suggestion
        coef_T = self.coef_.T if self.coef_.ndim == 2 else self.coef_
```
